# Where pyiceberg's extra time goes, on apache-polaris.
# Generated by bench_breakdown.py. Same catalog object, same session,
# same URL at every depth, so each line differs from the one above it
# by exactly one thing.

  client      pyiceberg 0.12.0 on python 3.14.7
  iterations  120, after 5 discarded
  measured    2026-09-18T16:23:16Z

## One GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces, at three depths (microseconds)

  layer                      p50       p90     stdev    added p50    2xSEM  separable?
  transport only          1171.0    1456.5     772.9           --       --
  transport, no env       1107.9    1359.7     267.3        -63.2    141.1  NO -- noise
  + json.loads            1168.8    1404.4     246.0        +60.9     48.8  yes
  + pydantic              1175.2    1457.0    1093.9         +6.5    199.7  NO -- noise
  + client method         1274.6    1519.2     268.1        +99.3    199.7  NO -- noise

  A delta is called separable only when it exceeds twice the standard
  error of the mean of the noisier layer it is differenced against.
  Anything marked NO is this machine, not that layer, and must not be
  quoted as the cost of it.

  transport is 92% of the call; everything the library does on top of
  it is the other 8%.

## The same GET through the other client's HTTP stack

  layer                      p50       p90     stdev
  rust, reqwest            269.8     355.1      68.8
  python, requests        1171.0    1456.5     772.9

  Both are a GET to the same URL with the same bearer, body read and
  discarded, against the same server on loopback. The server's own
  time is inside both of them, so the difference between these two
  lines is the HTTP client and nothing else.

  transport gap      +901.2 us
  pyiceberg's own    +103.6 us  (the client method above transport)

## Startup, decomposed (milliseconds, p50 of 5)

  bare interpreter, `python3 -c pass`            9.7
  + import pyiceberg.catalog.rest              372.8
    of which, the import itself                363.1
  catalog construction (config + auth)           8.0

  The benchmark's cold start figure is larger than these lines add up
  to because the worker imports more than the client: yaml, the
  conformance harness's auth provider and this directory's own modules
  are all on the path before a request is made. The point stands
  either way -- the dominant term is importing Python code, and it is
  paid before the client does anything.
